name: They that troubled the churches with circumcision
charge: Preaching another gospel, subverting souls with a commandment the apostles never gave
summary: Certain men came down from Judaea and taught the brethren that except they were circumcised after the manner of Moses they could not be saved, and Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, so the matter went up to the apostles and elders at Jerusalem. There rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying it was needful to circumcise them and to command them to keep the law of Moses. The council gave its sentence and sent letters saying that certain which went out from them had troubled the brethren with words, subverting their souls, to whom they gave no such commandment. Paul told the Galatians that any man preaching another gospel is accursed, and that he that troubleth them shall bear his judgment.
offenseFull: Certain men came down from Judaea and taught the brethren that except they were circumcised after the manner of Moses they could not be saved, and Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, so they were sent up to Jerusalem to the apostles and elders about this question (Acts 15:1-2). These men came out from Judaea infiltrating the congregations and causing confusion, and the demand hung on four words, after the manner of Moses. Under Moses the sacrifice followed the circumcision on the eighth day, so the demand meant reestablishing the covenant with Abraham and then the covenant of Moses: back to the temple, back to the sacrifice law. At Jerusalem there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying that it was needful to circumcise them and to command them to keep the law of Moses (Acts 15:5). Paul calls these the false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage (Galatians 2:4). The doctrine took even the strongest: Titus, a Greek, meaning one of our own brought up in Greek customs and not a Caucasian, was not compelled to be circumcised (Galatians 2:3), yet he forsook Paul in the end, though he was an elder charged to ordain elders in every city (2 Timothy 4:10, Titus 1:5).

Paul calls that system the weak and beggarly elements the Galatians desired to go back into (Galatians 4:9-10), and Hebrews says why it was weak: the gifts and sacrifices could not make the man that did the service perfect as pertaining to the conscience, and that commandment was disannulled for its weakness and unprofitableness (Hebrews 7:18-19, Hebrews 9:9, Hebrews 10:1). The book says it another way: he that keeps the law brings offerings enough, and to depart from wickedness pleases the Lord (Ecclesiasticus 35:1-3). There is also a reason Peter turned the argument to the Gentiles. If

salvation required circumcision and animal sacrifice, the northern kingdom could never be saved at all; they were strangers from the covenants of promise, cut off when Jeroboam set up his own calves, his own priests, and his own feast (Ephesians 2:12, 1 Kings 12:26-29). Only through Christ could all twelve tribes receive it. So Peter said that God made choice that the Gentiles should hear the gospel by his mouth, that God put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith, and asked why they tempted God by putting a yoke upon the neck of the disciples which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear (Acts 15:7-10). That yoke is the covenant of animal sacrifice.
judgmentFull: The sentence of the council was that they trouble not them which from among the Gentiles are turned to God, but write to them that they abstain from pollutions of idols, from fornication, from things strangled, and from blood, since Moses is read in the synagogues every sabbath day (Acts 15:19-21). Those four were their main hang-ups; the rest they would learn where the law was already taught. The apostles and elders then sent chosen men of their own company, Judas surnamed Barsabas and Silas, with letters saying that certain which went out from them had troubled the brethren with words, subverting their souls, to whom they gave no such commandment (Acts 15:22-24). Why letters? The congregation was being infiltrated, so trusted men had to carry certification of what was actually taught, and when it was read the people rejoiced for the consolation (Acts 15:30-31).

Paul carried the same judgment into his letter, marvelling that they were so soon removed to another gospel, which is not another, but there were some that troubled them and would pervert the gospel of Christ; and though he himself, or an angel from heaven, preached any other gospel, let him be accursed (Galatians 1:6-9). He went to an extreme on purpose. There is no way back for a heretic who learned Christ and then changed the doctrine; after the first and second admonition such a man is rejected (Matthew 12:31-32, Titus 3:10). The apostles gave them no place by subjection, not for an hour, and did not debate them, because there are weak-minded people easily deceived (Galatians 2:5).

Stand fast in the liberty and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage; a man circumcised after that manner is a debtor to do the whole law, and they that are justified by that law are fallen from grace (Galatians 5:1-4). In Christ neither circumcision nor uncircumcision avails anything, but faith working by love, which is faith keeping the commandments (Galatians 5:6). A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump, and he that troubleth them shall bear his judgment, whoever he is (Galatians 5:9-10, Galatians 5:13-14).

lawsResolved.text: Duty and Purpose of the Church (section)

text.text: And certain men which came down from Judea taught the brethren, and said, Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.

When therefore Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, they determined that Paul and Barnabas, and certain other of them, should go up to Jerusalem unto the apostles and elders about this question.
But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.
And that because of false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage:
But neither Titus, who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised:
For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world, and is departed unto Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus unto Dalmatia.
For this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city, as I had appointed thee:
But now, after that ye have known God, or rather are known of God, how turn ye again to the weak and beggarly elements, whereunto ye desire again to be in bondage?
Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years.
For there is verily a disannulling of the commandment going before for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof.
For the law made nothing perfect, but the bringing in of a better hope did; by the which we draw nigh unto God.
Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience;

For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.
He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough: he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering.
He that requiteth a good turn offereth fine flour; and he that giveth alms sacrificeth praise.
To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to the Lord; and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation.
That at that time ye were without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world:
And Jeroboam said in his heart, Now shall the kingdom return to the house of David:

If this people go up to do sacrifice in the house of the Lord at Jerusalem, then shall the heart of this people turn again unto their lord, even unto Rehoboam king of Judah, and they shall kill me, and go again to Rehoboam king of Judah.

Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.
And he set the one in Beth–el, and the other put he in Dan.

And when there had been much disputing, Peter rose up, and said unto them, Men and brethren, ye know how that a good while ago God made choice among us, that the Gentiles by my mouth should hear the word of the gospel, and believe.
And God, which knoweth the hearts, bare them witness, giving them the Holy Ghost, even as he did unto us;
And put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith.
Now therefore why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?
Wherefore my sentence is, that we trouble not them, which from among the Gentiles are turned to God:
But that we write unto them, that they abstain from pollutions of idols, and from fornication, and from things strangled, and from blood.
For Moses of old time hath in every city them that preach him, being read in the synagogues every sabbath day.

Then pleased it the apostles and elders, with the whole church, to send chosen men of their own company to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas; namely, Judas surnamed Barsabas, and Silas, chief men among the brethren:
And they wrote letters by them after this manner; The apostles and elders and brethren send greeting unto the brethren which are of the Gentiles in Antioch and Syria and Cilicia:

Forasmuch as we have heard, that certain which went out from us have troubled you with words, subverting your souls, saying, Ye must be circumcised, and keep the law: to whom we gave no such commandment:
So when they were dismissed, they came to Antioch: and when they had gathered the multitude together, they delivered the epistle:
Which when they had read, they rejoiced for the consolation.
I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel:
Which is not another; but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.
But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed.
As we said before, so say I now again, If any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.
Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven unto men.

And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.
A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject;
To whom we gave place by subjection, no, not for an hour; that the truth of the gospel might continue with you.
Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.
Behold, I Paul say unto you, that if ye be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing.
For I testify again to every man that is circumcised, that he is a debtor to do the whole law.
Christ is become of no effect unto you, whosoever of you are justified by the law; ye are fallen from grace.
For in Jesus Christ neither circumcision availeth any thing, nor uncircumcision; but faith which worketh by love.
A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump.
I have confidence in you through the Lord, that ye will be none otherwise minded: but he that troubleth you shall bear his judgment, whosoever he be.
For, brethren, ye have been called unto liberty; only use not liberty for an occasion to the flesh, but by love serve one another.
For all the law is fulfilled in one word, even in this; Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.
And I, brethren, if I yet preach circumcision, why do I yet suffer persecution? then is the offence of the cross ceased.
I would they were even cut off which trouble you.
But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.
